If present, the skill treats it as settled truth, tiers its features into Now/Next/Later, and renders a self-contained kanban to roadmap.html. If absent, the skill must NOT interview or parse a pasted conversation — it routes to chat-to-approach, which owns conversation-to-structure including the grilling pass. Keeping one conversation parser in the suite prevents two skills drifting apart and prevents a roadmap built on ungrilled assumptions.

# Approach — TaskPal

## What we're building

A minimal solo-founder task app with a fast keyboard-first capture flow.

## Features

### User authentication
- Problem: Users need a secure private account to keep their tasks.
- Value: Unblocks all persistence and sync.
- Dependencies: database setup

### Quick capture
- Problem: Adding a task takes too many taps today.
- Value: A single keyboard shortcut captures a task from anywhere.
- Dependencies: user authentication

### Weekly review view
- Problem: Users lose track of what they finished.
- Value: A read-only weekly digest of completed tasks.
- Dependencies: none

## Constraints

- Use Postgres.
- Mobile-first.

## Principles

- Ship weekly.

## Open questions

1. Should the weekly review be emailed or in-app only? — affects notification work.

assertions.text: The agent detects ./docs/approach.md exists (references an artifact-scan preflight or equivalent detection) before choosing a path
The agent takes the approach path: it does NOT invoke or delegate to the grilling skill
The agent does NOT ask the user to paste a conversation and does NOT re-parse source conversation text
The agent asks light prioritisation questions to assign the approach doc's features to Now / Next / Later

The tiering is reasoned, not arbitrary: the agent justifies at least one tier placement against the prioritisation lens (value / effort / dependency / risk) — e.g. tiering user authentication toward Now because it blocks quick capture
A self-contained roadmap.html is written with three columns (Now / Next / Later) and no JavaScript
The three features from approach.md (user authentication, quick capture, weekly review view) each appear as a card
The open question about emailed vs in-app weekly review is carried forward into the Open Questions section verbatim
The finishing receipt notes the source was ./docs/approach.md and that it was left unmodified

evals.name: conversation-without-approach-doc-routes-out
evals.prompt:
turn this into a roadmap:

Me: I want to build a small habit tracker. Definitely need accounts so people can save streaks.
AI: Makes sense. What about reminders?
Me: Yeah reminders are a must, push notifications.
AI: And you mentioned analytics earlier?
Me: We talked about a stats dashboard but I'm not sure. Maybe later. Also I decided we're NOT doing social sharing, that's out of scope.
AI: Got it. Anything on onboarding?
Me: There should be some onboarding but I haven't thought it through.
evals.expected_output: Because ./docs/approach.md does NOT exist, the skill must not build a roadmap from the transcript. It stops and routes the user to chat-to-approach — which owns conversation parsing and the grilling pass — and offers to invoke it, explaining that the roadmap can be generated once alignment is captured.

assertions.text: The agent determines ./docs/approach.md does not exist
The agent does NOT write roadmap.html
The agent does NOT parse the transcript into a set of feature cards and does NOT assign Now / Next / Later tiers
The agent does NOT run a grilling pass itself on the ambiguous items (stats dashboard, onboarding)
The agent names chat-to-approach as the skill to run first, and offers to invoke it with the pasted conversation
The agent explains that re-running to-roadmap afterwards will produce the board, so the user understands this is a routing step and not a refusal
The agent does NOT create or write ./docs/approach.md itself
